name: Tarmalune
foundedNote: An Abeiran place with no Torilian founding date; it existed on Abeir long before arriving with Laerakond in 1385 DR. Originally Tarmhaven, a domain of the Dawn Titan Achazar.

events.title: Arrives on Toril
events.summary: The Spellplague's blue fire shatters the fortress Glaur and rips Laerakond across to Toril, where Faerûn calls it Returned Abeir.

events.title: Envoys to Neverwinter
events.summary: Tarmalune merchants arrive in Neverwinter to open permanent trade with Faerûn.

events.title: Titan's peace
events.summary: Dragons keep clear of the city, fearing the sleeping titan Achazar burning as a pillar of fire in its midst (Wailing Years, c.).

events.title: Returns to Abeir
events.summary: The Second Sundering takes the continent back (gone by 1486 by some accounts), leaving Faerûn short of silkroot and other goods.

description: The great port of the Windrise coast rivals Waterdeep in wealth and noise, a jaw-shaped city of tall, narrow stone houses closing around its harbor. At its heart a sleeping titan burns as a pillar of flame, and dragons give the place a wide berth. Its council of traders lets almost anything happen, and its markets claim to sell everything.

visual.notes: A crescent of tall narrow stone houses wrapping a deep harbor like closing jaws, a column of fire rising from the centre.

description: Harglast is the plainest of the Windrise Ports, a city of squat, sturdy dwarf-built stone ruled by a dragonborn Lord Merchant. Beneath it run catacombs, sewers, and secret ways deep enough to touch the Upperdark. It ships stonework and dried figs, and its taverns ring with games of liar's dice.

visual.notes: Blocky, low grey stone buildings behind a thick wall on a harbor, with a dark catacomb entrance.

events.title: Rival of Tarmalune
events.summary: Larger than Tarmalune but less open, Imdolphyn's merchant-lords compete for Faerûnian trade and license privateers against pirates.

events.title: Wailing Years
events.summary: Dragonbane amber turns up across the continent and dragonborn slaves rise against their dragon masters (c. 1385–1395).

description: Second of the Windrise Ports and slightly larger than its rival Tarmalune, Imdolphyn climbs steep, winding cobbled lanes above the River Tantulph. Its shipyards are the finest on Abeir, and even its poor wear jewelry to keep up appearances. Every excuse earns a masquerade.

visual.notes: Ornate spired buildings stacked on a hillside above a river lined with shipyards and half-built hulls.

description: The smallest Windrise Port is a ramshackle town at the mouth of the River Sundarra, the place the other ports' merchants go to retire or rest. It has no government, yet hired adventurers keep it the most peaceful of the five. Its only shrine is to Umberlee, and its kitchens prize the yellow-finned oponi.

visual.notes: A jumble of mismatched wooden and stone buildings at a river mouth with fishing piers.

description: Sambral climbs from the Bay of Pearls in terraces joined by stairs, its streets paved with crushed oyster shell and too steep for carts. Its swaggering bravo troupes double as police and feud for fame. Above all of it rises the Nacre Tower of the Pearl Citadel, and every house smells of perfume.

visual.notes: Stepped terraces climbing from a bay, linked by stairs; a slender pearly tower atop a citadel at the summit.

foundedNote: An Abeiran place with no Torilian founding date; it existed on Abeir long before arriving with Laerakond in 1385 DR. The oldest dragon realm of Laerakond.

events.title: Djerad Kusold's revolt
events.summary: Dragonborn armed with dragonbane amber kill nearly a quarter of the realm's dragons before the dracolich Melauthaur destroys their fortress (c.).

events.title: Tarmalune traders
events.summary: Windrise merchants begin to brave the jungle empire for relics and rare herbs.

events.title: Returns to Abeir
events.summary: The Second Sundering takes the continent back (gone by 1486 by some accounts), leaving Faerûn short of silkroot and other goods.

description: The Jungle Empire has no roads and no towns, only monster-thick rainforest and rivers ruled by dragons under the dracolich Melauthaur and his twenty overdragons. Broken piers and vine-choked ruins on its coasts recall the humanoids who once lived there. Dragonborn are barred since their failed rising.

visual.notes: Dense jungle with a ruined stone pier on the shore and a dragon silhouette coiled atop a crumbling ziggurat.

name: Fimbrul
foundedNote: An Abeiran place with no Torilian founding date; it existed on Abeir long before arriving with Laerakond in 1385 DR. The Howling Mountains where the last Dawn Titans fell asleep after the War of Fang and Talon.

events.title: Oni war bands
events.summary: Oni gather Fimbrul's scattered orc tribes into war bands and lead them against the giants.

events.title: Relmaur's border war
events.summary: The underground dragonborn kingdom of Relmaur fights orcs spilling south from Fimbrul and holds the upper hand.

events.title: Returns to Abeir

description: The Land of Giants is a range of the Howling Mountains locked in endless winter, where the last primordials sleep inside the peaks. Earth giants, half-wild orcs, and a few dwarves share it, united only in driving out dragons. Darrawn is its one true city.

visual.notes: Jagged snowbound peaks with a giant-scale stone hall in a pass; one peak faintly glowing as a sleeping titan.
